documents.title: Single-cell chromatin accessibility atlas decodes bone development, diseases, and regeneration.
documents.abstract: Bone development, homeostasis, and regeneration are governed by complex, dynamic gene regulatory programs, and these processes are disrupted in numerous skeletal diseases. The epigenetic landscape-particularly chromatin accessibility-dictates transcription factor binding and gene expression, which fundamentally shape bone cell fate and function. In recent years, single-cell chromatin accessibility technologies, most notably single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq), have revolutionized bone epigenome research and enabled single-cell resolution dissect

documents.title: A Traditional Chinese Medicine Knowledge Graph for Hypertension With Emotional Comorbidity: Development and Blinded Question-Answering Evaluation.
documents.abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) literature on hypertension with anxiety, depression, or insomnia contains descriptions of syndrome patterns, treatment principles, formulas, and herbs. A focused knowledge graph can organize these associations and their sources, but its contribution to generated answers requires separate evaluation.

documents.title: Integration of genotyping by sequencing and machine learning for genome-wide identification of informative markers for body weight in broiler chickens.
documents.abstract: Identifying associations between single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and economically important traits is fundamental to modern poultry breeding programs. However, genome-wide studies based on commercial high-density SNP arrays are often prohibitively expensive, particularly for large populations and in resource-limited settings. Therefore, this study employed a cost-effective genotyping-by-sequencing (GBS) approach combined with two ensemble machine learning algorithms, Random Forest (RF) and Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), to identify informative markers of body weight (BW) at hatch, 3 w

documents.title: Lessons From CABBI: Advancing Vegetative Oil Production in C4 Crops Through a Vertically Integrated DBTL Framework.
documents.abstract: The global demand for renewable liquid fuels and biobased chemicals has intensified interest in engineering high-biomass C4 grasses to accumulate triacylglycerol (TAG) in vegetative tissues. Achieving this goal requires coordinated solutions across molecular biology, crop science, chemical engineering, and life cycle assessment, disciplines that rarely operate within a single research program. documents.title: Phenologs at knowledge-graph scale: a mouse-to-slime-mold catalog of candidate genes for thousands of human diseases.
documents.abstract: Model organisms carry decades of systematic gene-phenotype annotation, but connecting those annotations to human disease is rarely straightforward. Phenologs offer a principled way to bridge this gap. A human disease and a model-organism phenotype are phenologs when their associated genes, linked by orthology, overlap more than expected by chance, so the genes of one become candidates for the other. documents.title: OmniVira: a knowledgebase of source-linked evidence on viral spillover and cross-species transmission.
documents.abstract: Zoonotic viral emergence poses persistent challenges to global health, yet evidence relevant to spillover and cross-species transmission is dispersed across surveillance, epidemiological, experimental, mechanistic, and genomic studies. Here, we present OmniVira (https://omnivira.org/), a curated knowledgebase that transforms literature-derived findings into structured, traceable, and reusable OmniVira Evidence (OVE) records. documents.title: Early Prediction and Prognosis in Acute Kidney Injury Using a Biomarker-Aware Transformer: Retrospective Multicenter Study.
documents.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common, life-threatening complication among hospitalized patients. Timely prediction is crucial for prevention, while accurate prognosis following onset is essential for guiding care. Although electronic health records (EHRs) provide rich longitudinal data, their high dimensionality, heterogeneity, and temporal complexity pose challenges for traditional machine learning.

documents.title: Meta Mesh Ontology for Cross-Domain Mental Health Knowledge Integration: Development and Evaluation Study.
documents.abstract: Psychiatric diagnostic practice faces persistent challenges in adequately capturing the complexity, heterogeneity, and dynamic nature of mental disorders. Conventional categorical classification systems such as the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition (DSM-5) and the International Classification of Diseases, 11th Revision (ICD-11) rely on rigid symptom-based criteria that often fail to represent multifactorial etiologies, dimensional symptom profiles, and high rates of comorbidity. documents.title: scSpatial: an atlas for single-cell spatial omics.
documents.abstract: Single-cell spatial omics (SCSO) has reshaped spatial profiling by enabling simultaneous molecular characterization and spatial mapping at single-cell resolution, providing insights into cellular identities and tissue architecture within native biological contexts. By integrating spatial coordinates with molecular profiles and cell identities, SCSO datasets have been widely used to construct spatially resolved cell atlases, characterize disease-associated tissue remodeling, and map disease-relevant cell populations. However, these SCSO datasets remain fragmented across individual publications,

documents.title: AI-Empowered Multimodal Data Integration and Knowledge Discovery for Pharmacovigilance.
documents.abstract: Biomedical artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly relies on heterogeneous data sources, yet differences in data structure, terminology, evidence quality, and provenance complicate their integration into reliable knowledge resources. Here, we develop an evidence-aware framework for processing and integrating heterogeneous pharmacovigilance data from FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) reports, biomedical literature, clinical trials, and electronic health records in Mass General Brigham. documents.title: The Drosophila Secretome.
documents.abstract: Secreted proteins are synthesized within the cell and actively transported outside, where they contribute to development, physiology, immunity, and cell-cell communication. In Drosophila melanogaster , many secreted proteins are evolutionarily conserved, making this species a powerful model for studying human development, cancer, neurobiology, and immune regulation. To assemble the Drosophila secretome, we systematically analyzed all fly protein sequences with computational tools, integrating FlyBase, UniProt and Gene Ontology annotations, and incorporating large-scale proteomics datasets. documents.title: Precision Nutrition and Health Outcomes Across the Lifespan.
documents.abstract: Precision nutrition is an emerging paradigm that seeks to tailor dietary recommendations and interventions based on individual and population characteristics. Although advances in multi-omics, wearable sensors, and artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) have accelerated discovery, translation into practice remains limited by fragmented evidence across life stages and insufficient integration of knowledge regarding systems biology and other influences on health. documents.title: PIANO enables generative modeling of gene expression and scales multi-omics integration to 100 million cells.
documents.abstract: Single-cell RNA technologies enable the routine acquisition of transcriptomic atlases. However, these molecular profiles are influenced by overlapping sources of variation. Since these covariates confound comparisons, data integration is the first step in most analyses. Three challenges remain: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells, and modeling how covariates influence gene expression. documents.title: gcPathogen 2.0: an expanded multi-omics database advancing global pathogen surveillance and One Health research.
documents.abstract: Launched in 2024, gcPathogen established a critical foundation for the genomic surveillance of human pathogens. Here, we present gcPathogen 2.0, a major multi-omics update designed to address key analytical bottlenecks, including the integration of genomic and transcriptional profiles, systematic tracking of cross-habitat distribution, and large-scale discovery of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs). This release expands coverage from 1134 to 1506 pathogenic species, spanning 557 bacteria, 508 fungi, 258 viruses, and 183 parasites, and increases total genomic records past 2.3 million. documents.title: Metabolomics Subcenter (Met-SC): an integrated metabolomics database and analysis platform.
documents.abstract: The rapid growth of metabolomics data has increased the need for integrated storage, analysis, and reuse. Here, we present Metabolomics Subcenter (Met-SC) V1.0 (https://metabolomics.dicp.ac.cn/), an integrated database and platform for standardized data deposition, spectral-resource management, online analysis, and disease-focused knowledge mining. The deposition framework captures project, sample, pretreatment, and instrument metadata across chromatographic, capillary electrophoresis-mass spectrometry, and nuclear magnetic resonance workflows. documents.title: InterPro: the protein sequence classification resource in 2027.
documents.abstract: InterPro (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro) is a freely accessible resource for the classification of protein sequences. It integrates predictive models, known as signatures, from multiple member databases to classify sequences into families and to predict the presence of domains and functionally important sites. The InterPro database provides annotations for hundreds of millions of sequences, ensuring extensive coverage of UniProtKB, the standard repository of protein sequences, and includes mapping to several other major resources, such as Gene Ontology, the Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe),

documents.title: Crystalline silica particles exposure modulated miRNA expression profiles in human macrophage-like THP-1 cells.
documents.abstract: Occupational and environmental exposure to crystalline silica particles is a major global health concern linked to silicosis, pulmonary fibrosis, autoimmune disease, and lung cancer. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) regulate gene expression post-transcriptionally and are emerging as potential effect biomarkers of exposure in human biomonitoring studies. To identify intracellular and extracellular miRNAs responses to silica-particle exposure in human THP-1 derived macrophages, differentiated THP-1 derived macrophages were exposed to 0-300 µg/mL crystalline silica particles for 24 h. documents.title: Development of a Knowledge Map for Managing Symptoms of Graft-Versus-Host Disease in Patients Undergoing Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation.
documents.abstract: Graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) remains a critical complication affecting patients undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), with multifaceted symptoms requiring systematic management. Current clinical practices lack structured tools to guide nurses in addressing GVHD-related symptoms across diverse organ systems. This review aims to synthesize evidence on GVHD symptom management to construct a knowledge graph, enhancing nursing interventions and improving patient outcomes.

documents.title: Cutibacterium acnes induces T-cell extracellular traps with distinct proteome programs.
documents.abstract: Cutibacterium acnes is a common skin commensal associated with acne pathogenesis. In this study, we investigated whether acne-associated (denoted as CA) (HL043PA1) and healthy skin-associated (denoted as CH) (HL110PA3) C acnes strains differentially induce extracellular traps (ETs) in human neutrophils (neutrophil ETs) and T helper 17 cells (T-cell ETs [TETs]) and defined their proteomic and functional properties. documents.title: Reframing QSP: AI-Driven Multi-Modal Data as a New Measurement Layer.
documents.abstract: Quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) provides a mechanistic framework for integrating biological and pharmacological knowledge in drug development. Simultaneously, advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly in multi-modal data analysis, are transforming how biological information is derived. I argue that AI should not be viewed as a data integration tool, but as a new layer of quantitative measurement generation. This reframing positions QSP as a foundational model of biology, used here in a conceptual rather than technical sense, and AI as a source of quantitative inputs.

documents.title: PDBe-SIFTS: An open-source tool for Structure Integration with Function, Taxonomy, and Sequences, featuring improved alignment, scoring scheme, and accelerated search.
documents.abstract: Structure integration with function, taxonomy and sequences (SIFTS) provides residue-level mappings between UniProt Knowledgebase sequences and Protein Data Bank structures and has historically been generated through internal Protein Data Bank in Europe (PDBe) pipelines. Here, PDBe-SIFTS is presented as a fully open-source, locally deployable implementation of this mapping framework. The pipeline combines fast, scalable sequence search using MMseqs2, an improved bounded scoring scheme for ranking candidate mappings, and residue-level mapping refinement based on backbone connectivity. documents.title: EchoGO: annotation-context-aware functional interpretation of transcriptomic data.
documents.abstract: Functional enrichment of transcriptomic datasets can be constrained by incomplete annotation, uneven identifier recognition, and uncertainty about which organism annotation resource provides the most informative functional context. EchoGO is a reproducible downstream framework that retains target GOseq enrichment as the primary functional evidence while evaluating the same transcriptomic response across researcher-selected organism annotation contexts using experiment-specific backgrounds. documents.title: Closed-loop cognitive state control: a hypothesis framework for real-time estimation, stabilization, and recovery of task-specific high-performance cognitive states.
documents.abstract: Human performance often fails not because latent capacity is absent, but because access to high-functioning cognitive states is unstable under fatigue, distraction, overload, and pressure. This hypothesis paper proposes closed-loop cognitive state control-informally, supercognition-as a neuroengineering objective: rapid entry into, stabilization of, and recovery of an individual's highest available task-specific cognitive state. documents.title: HuRInterDB: A Database Exploring the Landscape of lncRNA-Protein Interactions.
documents.abstract: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) possess diverse biological functions and play key regulatory roles in biological processes by interacting with other biomolecules, such as proteins, RNAs, and the genome. High-throughput RNA-interaction experiments have generated large volumes of lncRNA-protein interaction records. The fragmented deposition of these records across disparate public databases complicates unified retrieval and integrative analysis. documents.title: Identification of metabolic vulnerabilities and synthetic lethal targets utilizing artificial intelligence-driven precision medicine.
documents.abstract: Cancer metabolism is highly plastic, and most attempts to turn that plasticity into a therapeutic target fail for a specific, recurring reason: a computational prediction of a metabolic vulnerability is not the same evidentiary object as an experimentally confirmed one, and the two are routinely discussed as if they were interchangeable. This review takes that distinction as its starting point rather than its conclusion. documents.title: Sustainable nutrition: integrating food systems, environmental science, and diet to advance public and planetary health.
documents.abstract: Nutrition science has traditionally focused on dietary intake, nutrient metabolism, physiology, and health outcomes. Although these domains remain fundamental, advancing public health increasingly requires understanding nutrition within the broader systems that shape food production, processing, access, consumption, and environmental sustainability.
